title: Personal Credit Cards: Points Remaining on a Card Being Closed
content:
The quantity of points a closing cash-out on Personal Credit Cards deals with is the card's remaining points, tallied from the card's ledger at the moment of handling.

## Tally

Start from the sum of all points ever awarded to the card on its purchases; from it are subtracted the points spent in any previous redemption and the points written off the card, whether by forfeiture or by clawback after a merchant refund. What is left is the card's remaining points.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger)

| Ledger entries | Points |
|---|---|
| Awarded on purchases | 18420 |
| Spent in a previous redemption | 6000 |
| Written off by refund clawbacks | 215 |
| Remaining points | 12205 |

The tally uses the ledger entries themselves, so every earlier redemption and write-off, on whatever date, is taken into account.
